question: Should OpenClaw adopt this repository-wide, fail-closed localization coverage manifest and required CI gate as the approved foundation for the five-part localization program?
rationale: The patch creates persistent cross-owner governance, a new package and environment-driven locale behavior, and a repository-wide check; code review alone cannot decide whether those product and release-policy contracts should exist.

options.title: Sponsor the governance contract
options.body: Approve the RFC direction, assign the relevant CLI/UI/Gateway/docs/CI owners, and require this slice to be rebased onto accepted predecessors with exact-head proof.

options.title: Narrow the proposal
options.body: Keep only a bounded contributor guide or existing-surface validation improvements and defer the global manifest and fail-closed check until ownership is agreed.

options.title: Defer the program
options.body: Leave the current localization behavior unchanged until a maintainer-owned roadmap and rollout plan are available.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the governance contract
recommendation.body: Approve the RFC direction, assign the relevant CLI/UI/Gateway/docs/CI owners, and require this slice to be rebased onto accepted predecessors with exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identifiable author of the full ordered foundation series and can coordinate the requested sponsorship decision with the affected current-main owners.
